headline: Atlassian exploitation lands alongside a live credential campaign and a spreading AI-infrastructure botnet
standfirst: A critical unauthenticated file-access flaw in Atlassian's Data Center products is being exploited after public proof-of-concept details, while U.S. authorities warn that the FortiBleed credential-harvesting campaign is still active. Also in today's selection: a maximum-severity SonicWall gateway flaw, an unpatched remote code execution bug in LLM caching software, a crypto-mining botnet on thousands of AI servers, a utility breach covering 400,000 accounts, eight malicious npm packages, and detention of a suspected ShinyHunters figure.
bodyMarkdown:
## Actively exploited

The day's lead is CVE-2026-21589 [[s18]], an arbitrary file-access flaw rated 9.3 Critical under CVSS 4.0, affecting Bitbucket, Confluence, Jira Service Management, Jira Software, Bamboo and Crowd Data Center, Crucible and Fisheye. The supplied vector is network-reachable with no privileges and no user interaction required, and the NVD description describes an unauthenticated remote attacker reading specific files inside the web application root directory — bounded by a real precondition: the attacker must already know the exact file name and path, and cannot enumerate or list directory contents. The same description notes that some configurations hold sensitive files, which is what makes this highly severe; it is classified CWE-552. The story text explicitly reports exploitation in the wild, tied by the headline to a public proof-of-concept release. Worth calibrating: the supplied KEV enrichment returns a confirmed catalog miss, which is a statement about the catalog as supplied, not evidence that exploitation has not occurred — the story's own reporting is what supports in-the-wild use here. The affected-versions field lists fix versions for several of the product lines but is truncated, so treat that list as partial.

The FBI and Secret Service say FortiBleed remains an active threat [[s21]], targeting internet-facing FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways, with 86,644 Fortinet device credentials amassed. The excerpt attributes the campaign's leverage to reused or leaked credentials and legacy SHA-256 password storage. No CVE is attached to this story. Analysis: if the entry condition is credentials that are still valid rather than an unpatched bug, then patching alone does not change the exposure — but the supplied excerpt is truncated, so the full mechanism and any advisory guidance are not available to us here.

Separately, the PoeLLM malware family has infected more than 3,400 servers to expand a cryptocurrency-mining botnet [[s6]]. The campaign, tracked as Canto Incognito, targets exposed AI and LLM infrastructure and is described as financially motivated. Its overlap in target class with the unpatched LMCache flaw below is the pattern worth noting: exposed model-serving and caching infrastructure is now attractive enough to sustain a mining operation.

## Vulnerabilities

SonicWall has released hotfixes for four flaws in its SMA1000 appliances, the gateways used for remote access to internal networks and applications [[s2]]. The most serious is rated 10.0 on the CVSS scale and is a pre-authentication SSRF that lets an attacker without a login route requests through the appliance to reach internal functions. SonicWall states it has no evidence that any of the four flaws is being exploited. No CVE identifiers were supplied for these four flaws, so they carry no KEV or NVD context in this selection and cannot be matched against the one distinct CVE identifier present in the evidence.

An unpatched critical vulnerability in LMCache, the open-source layer that accelerates LLM servers such as vLLM, allows an attacker to run code on the cache server without authenticating, and no fixed version exists [[s5]]. The flaw sits in LMCache's multiprocess mode, where the cache runs as a standalone server that LLM workers reach over the ZeroMQ messaging library; the excerpt truncates at "a single network", so the full delivery condition is not available. No CVE identifier was supplied, and no severity score or remediation is given beyond the absence of a fix.

## Breaches

Southern Company is notifying customers that their utility account information was accessed by hackers [[s9]], covering Georgia Power and Alabama Power, with 400,000 accounts affected. The supplied excerpt is short: no initial access vector, dwell time, or attribution is provided, and none should be assumed from the utility sector alone.

## Research

Eight malicious npm packages were downloaded 40,767 times as part of a long-running supply-chain campaign delivering the Overlord RAT and an information stealer [[s1]]. The activity is codenamed MALFEX and assessed to be the work of a lone threat actor who has published 12 packages, eight of them malicious. The excerpt is truncated at that point, so persistence mechanisms, targeting and any registry response are not supplied. The takeaway that does survive truncation is scale over time: this is not a single burst of typosquatting but a publisher with a multi-package history.

## Industry

A teenager from Amman, Jordan, suspected of leading ShinyHunters has been detained and is reportedly cooperating with the FBI to identify other members of the group [[s13]]. The suspect uses the handle "Rey", and the detention occurred as the group was in the process of extorting a business unit recently divested by Boeing. Both the leadership claim and the cooperation are explicitly reported as suspected and reported rather than confirmed, and the excerpt does not establish what data was taken in that extortion or whether a demand was paid.

nvd.description: This is a vulnerability in Bitbucket Data Center, Confluence Data Center, Jira Service Management Data Center, Jira Software Data Center, Bamboo Data Center. Crowd Data Center, Crucible and Fisheye. This Arbitrary File Access vulnerability allows an unauthenticated attacker to access specific files within the web application root directory in affected versions. Exploitation requires prior knowledge of the target file's exact name and path; this vulnerability does not allow attackers to enumerate or list directory contents. In some configurations, there may be some sensitive files that make this highly severe. This vulnerability allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to access specific files within the web application root directory in affected versions. The vulnerability must be addressed for affected versions of: -- Bitbucket Data Center, introduced in version >= 4.6.0, fix versions: 9.4.26, 10.2.8, 10.5.1 -- Confluence Data Center, introduced in version >= 5.10.0, fix versions 9.2.26, 10.2.19 -- Crowd Data Center, introduced in version >= 2.11.0, fix versions 6.3.7, 7.0.3, 7.1.7, 7.2.4 -- Jira Software Data Center, introduced in version >= 7.1.0, fix versions 9.12.40, 10.3.26, 11.3.12 -- Jira Service Management Data Center, introduced in version >= 3.1.0, fix versions 5.12.40, 10.3.26, 11.3.12 -- Bamboo Data Center >= 7.0.1, fix versions 10.2.24, 12.1.12 -- Crucible, fix versions 4.9.15 -- Fisheye, fix version 4.9.15 -- Exploitation requires prior knowledge of the target file's exact name and path. The vulnerability does not include the capability to enumerate or list directory contents.
